h.d: Compact sets in Euclidean space have finite Lebesgue outer measure.
For any set E and ε > 0, there exists an open U ⊇ E with m*(U) ≤ m*(E) + ε. This follows from outer regularity (Lemma 1.2.12).
Lemma 1.2.12 (Outer regularity). m\*(E) = inf\{m\*(U) : E ⊆ U, U open\}.
Lemma 1.2.11: Every open set is a countable union of almost disjoint dyadic cubes. Note: every dyadic cube is nonempty Proof outline: 1.
A larger dyadic cube (coarser scale n) cannot be contained in a smaller dyadic cube (finer scale m) when d > 0. This is because the sidelength 2^(-n) > 2^(-m) when n < m.
At the same scale, dyadic cubes with different indices cannot have one contained in the other (since containment would imply empty interior for one).

files.s: In this (technical) epilogue, we show that various operations and properties we have defined for "Chapter 6" sequences {name}`Chapter6.Sequence` are equivalent to Mathlib operations.
